claim_ceiling: This profile evaluates CityMaker as an assessment system. It does not rate district sustainability outcomes, validate a city, certify standards compliance or prescribe a single composite score.

research_basis.title: Beyond the Checklist: Meta-Indicators for Evaluating Effectiveness of Neighbourhood Sustainability Assessment Tools
research_basis.conceptual_status: document-based conceptual framework; not empirically validated as a rating tool
research_basis.source_scope: comparison of eight neighbourhood sustainability assessment tools
research_basis.note: The 13 meta-indicators are the paper's analytical framework, not indicators directly prescribed by the cited ISO standards.

maturity_states.meaning: No evidence that the assessment system addresses this meta-indicator.
The theme is named, but definitions, rules or implementation evidence are absent.
A clear definition and evidence requirement exist, but operational use is not demonstrated.
A repeatable procedure is used in at least one defined workflow or pilot.
Observed implementation data and raw denominators are reported.
Independent reviewers or replication support the reported result in the declared context.

indicators.name: Sustainability Dimension Coverage
indicators.definition: Whether the assessment covers environmental, social, economic, institutional and technological dimensions without hiding material omissions or overrepresentation.
assessment_questions: Which sustainability dimensions are included?
Which are mandatory, optional, or absent?
What share of criteria or evidence burden is assigned to each dimension?
What material local priorities are not represented?
indicators.limitation: Coverage breadth is not evidence of actual outcome quality.

indicators.name: Resilience and Risk Integration
indicators.definition: Whether climate, hazard, infrastructure, economic and social risks, preparedness, service continuity and recovery are embedded in decision criteria.
assessment_questions: Are risks and continuity assessed as core or optional criteria?
Are local exposure and vulnerable groups represented?
Are event probabilities evidenced or merely assumed?
Are recovery and adaptation monitored?
indicators.limitation: Synthetic continuity oracle is not a local hazard or service reliability study.

indicators.name: Indicator Transparency and Clarity
indicators.definition: Whether definitions, units, system boundaries, thresholds, calculation methods, uncertainty and evidence requirements are explicit and consistently interpretable.
assessment_questions: Can a reviewer reproduce each metric?
Are units and functional units explicit?
Are thresholds and normalization disclosed?
Are unknowns, uncertainty and assessor discretion visible?
indicators.limitation: Schema and metadata completeness do not prove underlying physical truth.

indicators.name: Equity and Inclusion
indicators.definition: Whether outcomes, burdens, access, affordability, accessibility, culture, displacement and decision participation are represented across relevant affected groups.
assessment_questions: Which groups are represented and who is missing?
Are worst-served and distributional outcomes reported?
Are displacement and affordability safeguards hard constraints?
Can affected groups challenge assumptions and evidence?
indicators.limitation: No individual household geolocation or mobility surveillance is assumed.

indicators.name: Innovation and Technology Inclusion
indicators.definition: Whether digital and technological methods contribute to measurable outcomes, accessibility, transparency, monitoring or adaptive management rather than being counted as innovation for its own sake.
assessment_questions: Are technologies linked to stated outcome requirements?
Are offline/manual alternatives and failure modes represented?
Are privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability and maintenance included?
Does innovation improve local capability?
indicators.limitation: Presence of BIM, IoT, AI or a digital twin is not proof of better outcomes.

indicators.name: Governance and Policy Integration
indicators.definition: Whether assessment requirements align with local planning and statutory processes, institutional responsibilities, budgets, decision rights and accountability.
assessment_questions: Who is legally or operationally responsible for each decision?
Does the method map to actual planning and budgeting processes?
Are conflicts and approvals visible?
Are corrections and appeals traceable?
indicators.limitation: No municipal endorsement or statutory compliance is inferred from a synthetic model.

indicators.name: Stakeholder Participation
indicators.definition: Whether affected residents, workers, operators, institutions and marginalised groups can influence requirements, alternatives, evaluation criteria and corrective action.
assessment_questions: Who is affected, invited, represented and absent?
At what stages can participants influence decisions?
How are dissent and competing claims recorded?
What changed because of participation?
indicators.limitation: Attendance counts alone do not measure meaningful influence or consent.

indicators.name: Adaptability and Contextual Fit
indicators.definition: Whether the method can adapt to local climate, informality, settlement pattern, institutional capacity, resource constraints, legal context and data availability while retaining a clear comparison boundary.
assessment_questions: Which assumptions are context-specific?
Can methods operate with sparse or imperfect data without false confidence?
Are local methods additions disclosed?
Can the system distinguish local adaptation from changed metric definitions?
indicators.limitation: A synthetic Johannesburg template is not a validated Johannesburg model.

indicators.name: Cross-Sectoral Relevance
indicators.definition: Whether essential urban systems and their interdependencies are assessed together rather than as disconnected silos.
assessment_questions: Are housing, health, education, food, water, energy, mobility, ecology, materials and maintenance represented?
Are dependencies and common-cause failures explicit?
Can a service be traced to products, production, delivery, commissioning and maintenance?
indicators.limitation: A composition manifest is not proof the district has the declared capacity.

indicators.name: Scalability and Usability
indicators.definition: Whether assessment procedures remain usable, reproducible and proportionate across component, building, neighbourhood and city scales.
assessment_questions: What expertise and infrastructure are required at each scale?
Which methods are reusable across scales?
Where does performance or reproducibility break down?
What proportion of work is manual or custom?
indicators.limitation: Passing a small synthetic crate is not production-scale throughput.

indicators.name: Training and Implementation Support
indicators.definition: Whether assessor, planner, operator, tradesperson and community-facing roles can acquire and maintain the competence needed to apply the system correctly.
assessment_questions: Which roles need training and how much?
Are competency requirements and support materials explicit?
Can local teams maintain the system?
Is specialist dependence a bottleneck?
indicators.limitation: No assumption that automation eliminates skilled trades or specialist review.

indicators.name: Cost and Time Efficiency
indicators.definition: Whether the full cost and time required to collect evidence, model, consult, assess, review, update and monitor are visible and proportionate.
assessment_questions: What data collection and analysis time is included?
Are licence, survey, consultation, reviewer, training and monitoring costs included?
Are cost base year, currency and scope explicit?
Are implementation burdens distributed fairly?
indicators.limitation: No local prices or cost savings are asserted without source-backed evidence.

indicators.name: Monitoring and Post-Evaluation
indicators.definition: Whether assessment results are revisited after commissioning and operation, with feedback into corrective action, maintenance and updated plans.
assessment_questions: Are outcomes monitored after handover?
Are observation time, valid time, revisions and corrections retained?
Can assessed predictions be compared with measured outcomes?
Can communities report failures and observe corrective action?
indicators.limitation: A complete digital thread is not causal proof that a particular intervention caused an outcome.

maturity_policy.not_found_in_manual: Not evidence that a capability is absent; record as not evidenced and seek clarification
maturity_policy.independent_validation_rule: Requires independent reviewer/replay or separate replication in the declared context
maturity_policy.context_binding: Each observation binds tool/manual version, jurisdiction, project phase, evidence snapshot and assessor method
